sections.text: Brazil's Senate passed a constitutional amendment cutting the workweek from 44 to 40 hours, ending six-day working schedules. Championed by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, it passed by 75 votes to one. Rival Flávio Bolsonaro reversed earlier opposition to vote yes, whilst Senator Hamilton Mourão cast the sole dissenting vote.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The reform affects over 30 million workers. Backers argue rest improves well-being and productivity, whereas critics warn increased business costs could raise consumer prices. Politically, it provides Lula momentum ahead of the 25 October presidential run-off against Flávio Bolsonaro, who narrowly won the first round.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: No changes take effect before the 25 October run-off. Following promulgation, a 60-day grace period precedes reducing hours to 42, before reaching 40 hours over a year later. Bolsonaro has reportedly told business leaders he would review parts of the amendment if elected.

sections.text: Caroline Bailey from Trelogan, Flintshire, suffered severe abdominal pain she believed was caused by her contraceptive coil. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Microsoft, working with Japan's National Police Agency and Health-ISAC, dismantled a marketplace named YAM Store and phishing kits called CoGUI and Iron Man. Since January 2026, these platforms enabled over one billion malicious messages targeting more than 75,000 organisations globally.

sections.text: The cybercrime network generated tens of millions of dollars for operators by targeting consumers, healthcare organisations, and financial institutions in over 150 countries. sections.text: Microsoft disabled over 20,000 connected accounts, blocked more than 100,000 web domains, and seized domains powering the platforms to reduce phishing messages.
